nodes.name: Run request
nodes.notes: POST /webhook/guard-before-run — where a launcher knocks before dropping a job. THE RESPONSE NODE IS EXPLICIT: with `lastNode`, the answer was whichever branch finished last. With the shadow judge stopped, the guard answered allowed=null. A guard that says neither yes nor no guards nothing.

nodes.name: Real node state
nodes.notes: The probe READS the machine: container alive, port answering, memory consistent, model identity. No declared state is taken on trust. The token lives in an n8n credential of type Header Auth (Authorization / Bearer <token>), NOT in an environment variable: n8n blocks $env inside nodes by default, and unblocking it would hand every node the database password and the encryption key too. Unset the token on both sides and the API is open — fine on a loopback bind, careless on a LAN one.

nodes.name: Judge decides
nodes.notes: Two questions in ONE call: same latency as one, and the state is billed once. Measured: 1 question 0.24 s, 3 questions 0.25 s. RETRY: 3 attempts, 2 s apart — the API occasionally returns a 520 after 38 s or aborts the connection, and without a retry a network hiccup becomes a guard outage. The API key comes from an n8n credential of type Header Auth (Authorization / Bearer <key>), never from the workflow file.

nodes.name: Branch on thresholds
nodes.notes: Thresholds 0.90 and 0.20, and BOTH are set by measured margin, not by taste. On this machine, same state, four passes: a node with a model on a card answers node_unfit 0.11-0.12 (variance 0.01); a node with nothing on a card answers 0.94-0.96. A threshold at 0.10 sat exactly on the first cluster and sent an obvious case to the grey zone. At 0.20 the margin is 0.08 — eight times the variance. THAT is where determinism comes from; not from the model, and never from a rounder-looking number.

nodes.name: Hold off
nodes.notes: A job killed mid-way loses its whole budget. It is never interrupted: the caller is told to come back.

nodes.name: Swap
nodes.notes: The turnstile answers already_serving, served with its duration, or queued with the estimated wait — never a technical error.

nodes.name: Allow
nodes.notes: The guard says yes. The CALLER drops the job, not this workflow: a guard is not a launcher.

nodes.name: Grey zone: escalate

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ title: 'Guard before run: grey zone', message: 'node_unfit=' + $('Judge decides').item.json.answers.node_unfit.noul + ' work=' + $('Judge decides').item.json.answers.work_to_preserve.noul + ' — the judge does not decide, a human should', priority: 4, tags: ['warning'] }) }}

nodes.notes: Between 0.10 and 0.90 the judge is not clear enough. Nothing is decided in silence: a human is notified.

nodes.name: Allow after swap
nodes.notes: Allows only if the swap really completed. Queued or failed, the guard refuses.

nodes.name: Local judge in shadow

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ state: $('Build the state').item.json.state, questions: $('Build the state').item.json.questions }) }}

nodes.notes: The local model answers in parallel, WITH NO EFFECT WHATSOEVER on the branching. Its only job is to accumulate pairs (state, remote verdict, local verdict) for a future specialisation: a base checkpoint here scored near chance and answered 1.00 to a question AND to its opposite. onError continue: a shadow failure must never break the guard.

nodes.name: Pair up
nodes.notes: The specialisation corpus is built here, one decision at a time.

nodes.name: Store the pair
nodes.notes: Appends one line to the corpus on the node. `turnstile-cascade` reads it daily to compute agreement. onError continue: losing a pair must never break the guard.

nodes.name: Respond
nodes.notes: The only node that answers. The four decision branches converge here; the shadow branch never touches it.

nodes.name: Grey zone verdict
nodes.notes: A notification receipt is not a verdict. This node turns the escalation into an explicit refusal, so the four decision branches all answer in the same shape.
